## Natural history notes

A small harvestman characterized by its compact oval body, very long slender legs, and ornate mottled brown, tan, or darker markings that help it blend into bark, leaf litter, and vegetation. In Florida, the Ornate Harvestman is found in humid wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, swamps, gardens, parks, and areas with logs, bark, vines, and leaf litter. It is an omnivorous scavenger and small predator, feeding on tiny insects, dead arthropods, fungi, and organic debris; unlike spiders, it does not produce silk or venom and is harmless to people.
